# Count Blocked Rate-Limited Requests

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/count-blocked-rate-limited-requests)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

You are analyzing an in-memory request history for a web platform. Each record includes three fields: `timestamp` (an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp), `request_ip` (an IPv4 client address), and `host` (the requested hostname). The records are already sorted by `timestamp` in ascending order, and the whole history fits in memory.

For a request at time `t`, only earlier records whose timestamps satisfy $$t - T < s < t$$ are considered. A record exactly at $$t - T$$ is not within the window. Requests that are blocked are still kept in the history and can affect later decisions. If several records share the same timestamp, process them in their original input order.

Part 1 — per-IP limiting:  
A request from IP `x` is blocked when the number of earlier window records from `x` is at least `IPReqMax`.

Part 2 — combined per-IP and per-(IP, host) limiting:  
A request from IP `x` to host `h` is blocked when at least one of the following is true:

- the number of earlier window records from `x` is at least `IPReqMax`, or
- the number of earlier window records from `x` to `h` is at least `IPHostReqMax`.

If a request violates both rules, it counts as one blocked request.

Return an array of two integers: `[blocked_per_ip_only, blocked_combined]`. When `IPHostReqMax` is omitted or `null`, the second value is computed under the per-IP rule only.

Example 1:

```text
Input:
logs = [
  ["2025-07-01T00:00:00Z", "203.0.113.9", "api.site-a.dev"],
  ["2025-07-01T00:00:10Z", "203.0.113.9", "api.site-b.dev"],
  ["2025-07-01T00:00:20Z", "203.0.113.9", "api.site-a.dev"],
  ["2025-07-01T00:00:30Z", "203.0.113.9", "api.site-b.dev"],
  ["2025-07-01T00:00:31Z", "203.0.113.9", "api.site-a.dev"],
  ["2025-07-01T00:01:01Z", "203.0.113.9", "api.site-c.dev"]
]
T = 30
IPReqMax = 2
IPHostReqMax = null

Output: [3, 3]
```

Explanation: The requests at 00:00:20, 00:00:30, and 00:00:31 are blocked. The request at 00:00:30 is blocked even though 00:00:00 is exactly 30 seconds earlier, because that timestamp is outside the window.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

For each request you need to know how many earlier requests from the same IP and host fall strictly inside the window.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a sliding window with a deque or two pointers per (ip, host) key, since records are already sorted by timestamp.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Remember the window is open on the left (t - T < s), and blocked requests still count toward future windows.

</details>
